system.name: Votegral
system.one_liner: a coercion-resistant e-voting architecture that lets voters register real and fake credentials in person and anonymously tallies only the real votes

content.subject: how a voter's real and fake credentials are registered, activated, used to sign encrypted ballots, then anonymized and tallied

elements.name: Register
elements.role: phase 1 heading: check-in and printing of the real and fake credentials

elements.name: Activate
elements.role: phase 2 heading: preparing each credential's key pair for signing

elements.name: Vote
elements.role: phase 3 heading: signing an encrypted ballot with a credential

elements.name: Tally
elements.role: phase 4 heading: shuffling, discarding mismatches, and counting real votes

elements.name: Registration Log
elements.role: public ledger entry linking a voter's identity to their public tag R

elements.name: Real Credential
elements.role: printed credential holding tag R, true key pair (R,r), and a true proof

elements.name: Fake Credential
elements.role: printed credential holding the same tag R but key pair (F,f) and a false proof

elements.name: Real Vote
elements.role: encrypted ballot signed by the real key pair (R,r)

elements.name: Fake Vote
elements.role: encrypted ballot signed by the fake key pair (F,f)

elements.name: Ballot Log
elements.role: public ledger of every signed ballot, real and fake alike, each tagged with R or F

elements.name: Anonymized Registration Log
elements.role: the Registration Log after verifiable shuffle, holding only blinded credential tags

elements.name: Anonymized Ballot Log
elements.role: the Ballot Log after verifiable shuffle; ballots are kept or struck out depending on tag match

elements.name: Ledger (Public Bulletin Board)
elements.role: the shared public ledger holding all four logs

elements.name: verifiable shuffle
elements.role: the crossed-ribbon operation applied to both the registration and ballot logs before tallying

elements.name: shuffle proofs
elements.role: cryptographic evidence that the shuffle was performed correctly

relations.what: checking in writes the voter's identity-linked entry and public tag R to the Registration Log
printing the real credential embeds tag R with key pair (R,r) and a true proof
printing the fake credential embeds tag R but key pair (F,f) with a false proof
activating the real credential lets the voter sign an encrypted ballot with (R,r)
activating the fake credential lets the voter sign an encrypted ballot with (F,f)
the signed real ballot is recorded in the public Ballot Log
the signed fake ballot is likewise recorded in the Ballot Log
a verifiable shuffle blinds and reorders credential tags
the same verifiable shuffle reorders ballots, producing shuffle proofs
a ballot whose tag has no match in the anonymized registration log is struck out and discarded; a matching one is counted

steps.what: the voter checks in, writing an identity-linked entry (ID, public tag R) to the Registration Log
a real credential is printed carrying tag R, true key pair (R,r), and a true proof
a fake credential is printed carrying the same tag R but key pair (F,f) and a false proof
the voter checks out holding both credentials
the Registration Log and Ballot Log are both verifiably shuffled, blinding credential tags
ballots whose tag has no match in the anonymized registration log are discarded
only the remaining, tag-matched real votes are decrypted, counted, and the results published

content.key_idea: A voter's single public tag anchors two credentials, real and fake, both used to sign otherwise-identical encrypted ballots; only at tally does a verifiable shuffle anonymize tags and ballots so only tag-matched real votes get decrypted and counted.
content.reading_order: left to right through Register, Activate, Vote, Tally, dropping down into the Ledger boxes each phase writes to, then following the shuffle arrows into the two anonymized logs

palette.used_for: pale green fill of proof boxes (true proof, false proof, shuffle proofs)
pale yellow fill of the secret-key cells (r, f)
pale orange fill of the credential-tag/key cells (R, F) and the ballot cells
pale lavender fill of the Real/Fake Credential and Real/Fake Vote container boxes
pale blue fill of the Ledger's log sub-boxes (Registration Log, Ballot Log, and their anonymized counterparts)
pale pink shading marking the discarded (struck-out) ballot row in the Anonymized Ballot Log
gray fill of the ID cell in the Registration Log

style.stroke: thin black box outlines and arrows; a bright red strikethrough marks the one discarded ballot
style.arrows: thin black arrows and dotted leader lines linking a credential's tag to its origin, plus bold gray block arrows marking the shuffle step
style.font: sans-serif (Liberation Sans), bold for phase headers and log names, italic for numbered instructions and annotations
style.icons: a person silhouette for check-in; crossed-ribbon shuffle icons for the verifiable shuffle; a red X strikethrough for a discarded ballot

encoding.color_means: green marks zero-knowledge proof boxes; pale orange marks the R/F credential tags, keys, and ballots; lavender marks the four credential/vote container boxes; pale blue marks the ledger's log sub-boxes; pink shades the one discarded ballot
encoding.line_style_means: dotted lines trace a tag or ballot back to where it was produced; solid arrows show data being written into a log or carried to the next phase; bold gray block arrows mark the verifiable-shuffle step
encoding.state_means: real vs fake is told apart purely by the letter inside an identically-styled orange cell (R vs F) and by which credential/vote box it sits in, not by a different colour
encoding.marker_means: plain numbers under Register (1-4) and Tally (1-3) order each phase's sub-steps; a red X marks a ballot discarded for a non-matching tag
encoding.emphasis: the red strikethrough on the unmatched ballot in the Anonymized Ballot Log visually singles out the discard case right where the tally decision happens
reusable_patterns: parallel real/fake instances of the same box template (Credential, Vote) carried through matching Ledger logs, reunited only at a shuffle step drawn with a crossed-ribbon icon
weaknesses: real and fake items share the same orange cell colour and differ only by an R/F letter, so a reader skimming by colour alone could miss which ballot is genuine

summary: Figure 3 summarizes Votegral's full protocol for one voter across four phases. In Register, checking in (1) writes an identity-linked entry to the public Registration Log, then printing a real credential (2) and a fake credential (3) both embed the same public tag but different key pairs, (R,r) with a true proof and (F,f) with a false proof, before checking out (4). In Activate and Vote, each credential signs an encrypted ballot with its own key pair, and both signed ballots land in the public Ballot Log. In Tally, a verifiable shuffle (1) blinds and reorders both the Registration Log's tags and the Ballot Log's ballots together with shuffle proofs; ballots whose tag has no match in the anonymized registration log are discarded (2); and only the remaining, tag-matched real votes are decrypted, counted, and published (3).
summary_zh: 该图示Votegral协议：Register签到并打印真假两枚凭证(同一tag，密钥对分别为(R,r)/(F,f))；各凭证签名选票存入Ballot Log；Tally将两日志洗牌，丢弃tag不匹配选票，仅解密计数真选票并公布结果。
